_note: Board rows that are demonstrably not about the company, established by counting the raw r/wallstreetbets text in data/reddit/ rather than by judgement. Written by hand from the checks recorded in `evidence`; scripts/verify_overlap.py is what produces the candidates. Nothing here is removed from the archive — the archive records what ApeWisdom said, and editing it would destroy the only record of what it said. These are labels, not deletions.
_status: 2026 archive complete; 2021-2025 pass done for calibration and surfaced two further artefacts (IS, WW). 401 days of raw text were fetched and the per-day results kept in data/divergence_daily.json so the corpus itself need not be.

WW.evidence: Ranked #2 on 2024-04-14 with 119 mentions on a day when standalone WW appears in the subreddit zero times. WW.mechanism: Not established. 'ww' appears 386 times, essentially all inside www URLs, and the count of items containing www is the right order of magnitude but not the right number: 119/160, 92/137, 87/219 — ratios of 0.74, 0.67 and 0.40. DTE was provable because their 70 met our 69; this is not that, and saying 'they count URLs' would be a story fitted to three points.
WW.cause: unknown — the only certainty is that the row does not measure the company

NOW.evidence: All three spike windows are ServiceNow. 2026-07-22 ('$NOW earnings', 'Is anyone playing NOW earnings') is its Q2 print, and ApeWisdom's 231 equals the bare-uppercase count of 231 exactly. 2026-05-29 has 30 $NOW; 2026-05-21 has 9 plus 'NOW 7/17 120 C play'.
NOW.our_bug: NOW was in compare_counts.WORDLIKE, so our count saw only $NOW — 13 against ApeWisdom's 190 over five days. It is off the list now, which takes the count ratio from 0.07 to 1.46. That is a count fix, not a rank fix: the same change moves the median rank correlation 0.923 -> 0.902, because a ticker ranked far too low became one ranked somewhat too high. Bare uppercase NOW is still sometimes the English word ('NOW is the time'), so both series carry some of it and neither is correct.

calibration.top10_overlap_mean: 9.4 of 10, or 9.7 excluding the marked tickers
calibration.note: Every day of the 2026 archive now has the raw text behind it. Going from 21 to 43 to 103 days left the ratio at 1.09 throughout, which is what a stable instrument offset looks like. Disagreement concentrates on quiet days — the coldest third sits at 0.867 against 0.945 for the hottest — because a board of small counts is mostly ties and ties have no stable order. This is agreement between two independent counting rules, not accuracy: there is no ground truth here, and the only place either source can be called wrong is where the raw text settles it. Measured at top-20; at top-50 the median was 0.831.

audit.artifact_share_of_all_events: 6 of 260 = 2.3%, or 8 of 260 = 3.1% counting the two BE events
audit.not_in_the_event_set: DTE — top-50 on all 103 days, best rank #4, and zero spike events, because slang volume is high but flat
audit.also_found_by_divergence_scan: CC (0 spike events) and ALL (0 spike events, and our error too)
audit.found_by_divergence_scan: CC, ALL, ON, JUST — all four surfaced by scripts/divergence.py once the overlap reached 103 days, none of them producing a single spike event
audit.detectors: Two automatic tests, and neither is sufficient alone. Divergence finds tickers the two counting rules treat differently (DTE, BE, CC, ON, JUST). The dollar-sign test asks the text alone whether anyone ever writes $TICKER, and catches the ones both rules get wrong together (EU, SELF, TASK) plus nine more. Of 27 unambiguous real tickers not one sits at zero — the floor is ASTS at 1.3%. It convicts in one direction only: some $ usage does not clear a row, since BE carries 24 $BE among 632 matches and is still caps-lock English.
audit.coverage: Every board row now carries a record of whether it was ever counted against the raw posts: 1,861 tickers, 100% of the top 100 and 93% of the deep board, against 19% when the scan only went 50 deep. Depth 500 costs nothing — the intersection is over each item's own tokens, not over the candidate list — and 50 had made Deep risers, which are new to the board by definition, the least likely rows to have been checked.

our_own_errors._note: A file that catalogues only the other source's mistakes is the bias it warns about. Same method, turned on scripts/compare_counts.py. Measured on the 2026-08-07 window, 32,898 items, using the real counter including its WORDLIKE exemptions.

YOU.cause: YOU (Clear Secure) is not in WORDLIKE, so bare uppercase counts
YOU.severity: 5.3x high — worse on this day than ApeWisdom's DTE error is in relative terms

UP.actually: 'HERTZ ONLY GOES UP', 'SHUT UP AND EAT YOUR LETTUCE'
UP.cause: same — UP (Wheels Up) is not in WORDLIKE

IT.actually: unknown — we cannot see it at all
IT.cause: IT is in WORDLIKE, so only $IT counts, and nobody writes $IT

our_own_errors.conclusion: Neither rule is the truth. Ours is wrong on YOU and UP in exactly the way theirs is wrong on DTE, and wrong on IT in the opposite direction. What the second source buys is not accuracy but auditability: every number here can be taken back to the sentence that produced it, which is the only reason the five confirmed artifacts were findable at all. The disagreements are not noise to be corrected away — they mark where 'what counts as a mention' actually bites.
our_own_errors.open_question: YOU and UP could join WORDLIKE for consistency, at the cost of going blind to them the way we are blind to IT. That is the same trade NOW lost. Not changed without a decision.

ALL.actually: the English word — 'To ALL who bought HTZ', 'BAN ALL MENTION OF HTZ OR KOSPI'
ALL.cause: ALL is in WORDLIKE so we see nothing; ApeWisdom counts 19 of the 55, so it is wrong too, in the other direction
ALL.severity: blind, like IT — and their number is not right either, so neither series measures Allstate

scan_blind_spot._note: scripts/divergence.py ranks tickers by distance from the stable 1.13 offset. It finds errors the two rules make DIFFERENTLY. It is structurally blind to errors they make the SAME WAY, and that blindness is the more dangerous one, because agreement reads as confirmation.
scan_blind_spot.proof: EU is a confirmed artefact — the European Union, zero $EU, four false spike events — and its ratio is 1.20, sitting comfortably inside the normal band. Both rules count the bare uppercase word, so both are wrong in the same direction by the same amount, and the scan cannot see it. SELF and TASK are the same shape. Of the six confirmed artefacts the scan surfaces only DTE, BE and CC.
scan_blind_spot.implication: Two sources raise confidence only where their rules genuinely differ. Where they share an assumption — that a bare uppercase token is a ticker — a second source adds no protection at all, and combining or averaging them would hide that fact behind a number that looks corroborated. The three artefacts the scan misses were found by reading the text of flagged spike events, which is a different and non-automatable check.

five_year_preliminary.finding: The offset is not a fact about 2026. Across five years the usable captures give 1.08 and 0.900, against 1.09 and 0.918 for the 103 collected days.
five_year_preliminary.caveat: The three days that looked like violent disagreement — ratios 13.80, 0.00 and 0.14 — are all thin captures, not disagreement. See data/wayback/quality.json `thin`.
five_year_preliminary.status: 144 usable captures identified; raw text still downloading

five_year_calibration.finding: The offset is not a fact about 2026. Over five years it is 1.07 with a day-to-day sd of 0.042 — tighter than the 0.080 of the 103 densely-collected 2026 days, because these are spread across years rather than clustered in one quarter.
five_year_calibration.method_note: Excludes both defects in the captures: 11 frozen pages and 75 caught mid-reset. Including the thin ones put the spread at 0.14-13.80 and the sd at 1.172 — a five-year answer that read as violent instability when 144 of 161 days agree to within a few per cent.

verification_coverage._note: What the site puts on every row: whether anything ever counted it against the raw posts, and how much that is worth. The tier boundaries are measured, not chosen.

artefact_rate.note: 5.6% is the figure an unchecked row should carry, not 1.1%. The larger denominator is mostly rows of one mention, which are neither checkable nor consequential; the rate that matters is among rows loud enough to be read.

verification_coverage.why_16_days: At 16+ counted days the 90th percentile of deviation is 0.075 and at 1-2 days it is 0.419 — a row's ratio is worth roughly six times more when it has been seen that often. The middle bands are small samples and not monotonic (6-15 days has a wider p90 than 3-5), so they are one tier rather than three: the data supports two boundaries, not four.
